subject: Post-demo: cost & throughput test plan - Redwood vs CloudRidge hyperscaler
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Green <oliver@cloudridge.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Oct 2026 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: cost & throughput test plan - Redwood vs CloudRidge hyperscaler

Thanks again for taking the demo today — appreciated the thoughtful questions. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can validate economics and performance side-by-side.

What we heard (summary)
- Primary objectives: establish per-1M token unit economics, confirm 95th pct latency at target QPS, and measure effective cache-hit uplift on your prompt corpus.
- Constraints: data residency in us-west, ability to run a short pilot (3 days) against production-like prompts, and a preference to compare both hosted and private deployment modes.

Proposed comparison tests (high level)
1) 1M-token throughput test: run ~1M tokens end-to-end across 3 model variants (baseline FP16, int8 quantized, and a trimmed-serving variant). Measure tokens/sec, GPU utilization, and per-token cost.
2) Batching & tail-latency matrix: sweep batch sizes (1,4,8,16) at target QPS to capture median and 95th pct latencies.
3) Cache hit experiment: run your canonical prompt set (we'll seed with 10k unique prefixes) to measure prefix/KV cache hit rate and token savings.

What Redwood will provide
- Test plan doc (attached) with execution steps and metrics we will capture.
- A dedicated test pool for the run or guidance for a Private pilot depending on what you prefer.
- A preliminary cost model with example per-1M token buckets (see pricing-matrix.xlsx).

What we need from you to start
- A small representative prompt set (10k prompts) or a sanitized sample; link or SFTP access.
- A service account/temporary API key or a VPC peering window for private pilot.
- Target QPS and the SLO you want us to validate (recommended: 50 qps sustained, 200 burst).

Suggested timeline
- Confirm scope & credentials by Mon Oct 5
- Run tests Oct 6–7 (3x mini runs to validate variance)
- Sync Oct 8 with results and a refined cost sheet

Attachments: redwood-1mtoken-test-plan.pdf, pricing-matrix.xlsx

If that looks good I can schedule Ben (SE) and Marissa (pricing) to run the tests and join the result review. Next available slot for the sync: Fri Oct 8 10:00am PT.

Thanks,
Camila Reyes
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Oliver — quick answers and a small worked example to set expectations. I attached a sample-cost-breakdown.csv with the math; below is a short summary (ballpark, pre-run).

Assumptions used for the sample numbers
- Average prompt tokens: 100
- Average completion tokens: 250
- Effective cache hit rate (assumed): 65% (we'll measure this)
- Test duration: enough to reach 1,000,000 generated tokens after caching savings

Redwood (hosted) - sample per-1M tokens (USD, approximate)
- Baseline FP16: $85 / 1M tokens
- int8 quantized: $52 / 1M tokens
- trimmed-serving variant (aggressive KV/cache): $38 / 1M tokens

Hyperscaler managed endpoint (public pricing estimate)
- Baseline: $130 / 1M tokens
- Quantized offerings vary; practical numbers we've seen: $90–120 / 1M depending on instance type and batching windows (does not include egress)^1

Key notes
- These numbers are illustrative and sensitive to batching, model quality targets, and cache effectiveness. In particular, raising batch size improves amortized cost but increases tail latency — that's why we'll sweep batch-size vs 95th pct latency.
- The cache experiment is client-side: Redwood collects prefix/KV stats via request headers we add (no instrumentation in your model code). If you prefer, we can run an isolated VPC pilot with the same approach.
- For a private pilot sizing: a single 80GB A100-equivalent instance per variant for the test window is typical; we can reduce to a smaller instance for quantized variants. Ben can provide precise VM/GPU SKUs.

Next steps
- If you confirm the sanitized prompt set by Mon Oct 5, we will allocate the test pool and run the three variants Oct 6–7.
- I’ll schedule the Oct 8 sync; proposed agenda: test summary, per-1M token recalculation, latency matrix, cache-hit % and recommendations.

Related: HubSpot deal (linked), sample test data folder (linked in my earlier email).

Thanks,
Camila

1. Hyperscaler numbers are estimates assembled from public docs + prior customer benchmarks; we'll update with direct run numbers after the test.
